item.title: California union pushes work-from-home bill as Newsom calls state employees back to the office
item.description: The legislative proposal by the California union known as PECG would require state agencies to offer telework options “to the fullest extent possible” and mandate they disclose how much money they save by allowing remote work.

item.title: California sues websites that publish blueprints for 3D printer ghost guns
item.description: California law enforcement agencies seize about 11,000 ghost guns every year. The state now is suing websites that help people manufacture untraceable firearms.

item.title: EPA touts bipartisan efforts to clean up Tijuana River
item.description: EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin met with local and congressional leaders in San Diego on Thursday to tout the U.S. and Mexico's progress in cleaning up the polluted Tijuana River.

item.title: Will California lawmakers break their promise to child sexual abuse survivors?
item.description: In 2019, the Legislature and Gov. Newsom closed a loophole that allowed schools to avoid liability for child sexual abuse. Now the law is under threat.

item.title: Tax dollars should fund children’s education, not attorneys’ fees in child sex abuse cases
item.description: California school districts could be on the hook for about $3 billion in liability for child sexual abuse lawsuits. Up to 40% may go to trial attorneys.

item.title: ‘Little death bombs’: Illegal cannabis farms poison California’s forests. Who’s cleaning them up?
item.description: Even after legalization, illicit cannabis grows continue to pollute California’s public lands. And the contamination, new research shows, lingers.

item.title: CA’s illegal pot farms pollute public forests and watersheds
item.description: Illegal cannabis farms hidden inside California forests harm nearby wildlife, ecosystems and watersheds. But with little being done at the federal and state levels to clean up these sites fast enough, ecologists are sounding the alarm about the pollution the farms wreak on the state’s public lands. item.title: California gasta millones en base a datos de este rastreador de polución. ¿Quién se beneficia de su última actualización?
item.description: California está actualizando CalEnviroScreen, el sistema de seguimiento de la contaminación que ayuda a determinar qué comunidades reciben subvenciones ambientales. Los activistas afirman que el estado debería mejorar la herramienta y usarla con mayor frecuencia para reducir la contaminación.

item.title: La EPA promociona esfuerzos bipartidistas para limpiar el río Tijuana
item.description: El administrador de la EPA, Lee Zeldin, se reunió con líderes locales y del Congreso en San Diego para promocionar el progreso de Estados Unidos y México en la limpieza del contaminado río Tijuana.

item.title: California dirt bikers battled against desert preservation, spawning anti-environmental wars
item.description: Today’s anti-environmentalists follow tracks laid by the ‘Phantom Duck’ and the Barstow-to-Vegas Race, where thousands of bikers sped across open desert.
